title: The back door
logline: The tavern's back door — the one he used for twenty years to get to the garage — drawn from the front lot for once, small, at the building's side, with the garage's roof beyond it. The sign is above, out of frame.

panels.composition: The tavern from its front gravel lot in evening light, but the page's subject is the side: a narrow gap between the building and the fence where a plain door with a bare bulb over it leads back, and beyond the gap, the garage's roof and its one window. A man from behind, blue plaid, walking into the gap. The sign is above the top edge; its glow is on the gravel.

characters.pose: from behind, walking into the gap

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, a wooden tavern seen from its front gravel lot in evening light with a narrow gap along its side where a plain back door with a bare bulb leads toward a garage roof with one window, a man in blue plaid flannel seen from behind walking into the gap, the glow of an unseen sign on the gravel, no words
image.notes: The sign's name reserved; it is above the frame. Its glow only.

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run

notes: The way in, seen from the front. The sign's glow, not the sign.
